extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters, agency heads, OMB/OIRA staff, and regulatory policy advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies on planning, developing, reviewing, and publishing regulations, including OIRA centralized review, public participation, cost–benefit assessment, intergovernmental coordination, and transparency under Executive Order 12866 (1993).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory philosophy — necessity and net benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should promulgate only such regulations as are required by law, are necessary to interpret the law, or are made necessary by compelling public need; in deciding whether and how to regulate, agencies should assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives, including the alternative of not regulating; costs and benefits shall include quantifiable measures and qualitative measures; agencies should select approaches that maximize net benefits (including economic, environmental, public health and safety, distributive impacts, and equity), unless a statute requires another approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching standard guiding when agencies should regulate and which approach to choose; it requires consideration of both quantitative and qualitative effects and explicit attention to distributive impacts and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1 — identify the problem and assess its significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify the problem that it intends to address (including, where applicable, the failures of private markets or public institutions that warrant new agency action) as well as assess the significance of that problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must frame regulatory actions by clearly stating the problem and why agency action is warranted, including market or institutional failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2 — examine whether existing law created the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall examine whether existing regulations (or other law) have created, or contributed to, the problem that a new regulation is intended to correct and whether those regulations (or other law) should be modified to achieve the intended goal more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agencies to consider reforming or removing prior rules that may have caused or exacerbated the problem before adopting new prescriptive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3 — identify and assess alternatives to direct regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess available alternatives to direct regulation, including providing economic incentives to encourage the desired behavior, such as user fees or marketable permits, or providing information upon which choices can be made by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonregulatory or market-incentive approaches must be evaluated as potential means to achieve policy objectives with potentially lower burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4 — consider degree and nature of risks when prioritizing
rubrics_metrics.description: In setting regulatory priorities, each agency shall consider, to the extent reasonable, the degree and nature of the risks posed by various substances or activities within its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessment (relative magnitude and nature of risks) should inform which regulatory actions receive priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 5 — design cost‑effective regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency determines that a regulation is the best available method of achieving the regulatory objective, it shall design its regulations in the most cost-effective manner to achieve the regulatory objective; consider incentives for innovation, consistency, predictability, the costs of enforcement and compliance, flexibility, distributive impacts, and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design should minimize costs while achieving objectives and encourage innovation and predictability; consider enforcement/compliance burdens and distributional effects across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 6 — assess costs and benefits and adopt only upon reasoned determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall assess both the costs and the benefits of the intended regulation and, recognizing that some costs and benefits are difficult to quantify, propose or adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that the benefits of the intended regulation justify its costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a documented, reasoned judgment balancing costs and benefits, including qualitative factors where quantification is infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 7 — base decisions on best reasonably obtainable information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall base its decisions on the best reasonably obtainable scientific, technical, economic, and other information concerning the need for, and consequences of, the intended regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-making must rely on current best-available evidence and analysis; agencies should seek and use robust information sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 8 — prefer performance objectives and consider alternative regulatory forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess alternative forms of regulation and shall, to the extent feasible, specify performance objectives, rather than specifying the behavior or manner of compliance that regulated entities must adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, set outcomes-based standards enabling flexibility in compliance rather than prescriptive mandates; analyze alternative regulatory instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 9 — consult and assess effects on state, local, and tribal governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever feasible, agencies shall seek views of appropriate State, local, and tribal officials before imposing regulatory requirements that might significantly or uniquely affect those governmental entities; assess effects of Federal regulations on them, including availability of resources to carry out mandates, and seek to minimize burdens that uniquely or significantly affect such entities; harmonize Federal regulatory actions with related State, local, and tribal functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intergovernmental consultation and impact assessment are required for rules affecting subfederal governments, with an aim to minimize unique burdens and improve harmonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 10 — avoid inconsistency, incompatibility, and duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall avoid regulations that are inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative with its other regulations or those of other Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should coordinate to prevent conflicting or overlapping rules across the federal regulatory landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 11 — tailor regulations to impose least burden, considering cumulative effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall tailor its regulations to impose the least burden on society, including individuals, businesses of differing sizes, and other entities (including small communities and governmental entities), consistent with obtaining the regulatory objectives, taking into account, among other things, and to the extent practicable, the costs of cumulative regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes proportionality and attention to small businesses/communities and the aggregate burden of multiple regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 12 — draft regulations simply and clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall draft its regulations to be simple and easy to understand, with the goal of minimizing the potential for uncertainty and litigation arising from such uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain drafting reduces ambiguity, compliance cost, and legal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'regulation' and scope/exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Regulation' or 'rule' means an agency statement of general applicability and future effect, which the agency intends to have the force and effect of law, that is designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe the procedure or practice requirements of an agency; it does not include: (1) rules issued in accordance with formal rulemaking provisions of 5 U.S.C. 556, 557; (2) rules that pertain to a military or foreign affairs function (except procurement and import/export non-defense articles/services); (3) rules limited to organization, management, or personnel matters; or (4) other categories exempted by the Administrator of OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which agency actions are subject to the order's planning and review requirements and identifies common exempt categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'significant regulatory action'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Significant regulatory action' means any regulatory action that is likely to result in a rule that may: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State/local/tribal governments or communities; (2) create a serious inconsistency or interfere with another agency's action; (3) materially alter budgetary impact of entitlements, grants, user fees, or loan programs or rights/obligations of recipients; or (4) raise novel legal or policy issues arising out of mandates, the President's priorities, or the principles of this Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This threshold determines which rules are subject to heightened OIRA review and additional analytic requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Regulatory Agenda minimum content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall prepare an agenda of all regulations under development or review; the description of each regulatory action shall contain, at a minimum, a regulation identifier number, a brief summary of the action, the legal authority for the action, any legal deadline for the action, and the name and telephone number of a knowledgeable agency official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Unified Agenda is the primary public planning document; agencies may incorporate information required under 5 U.S.C. 602 and 41 U.S.C. 402.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plan — required elements (agency's Regulatory Plan content)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the Unified Agenda, each agency shall prepare a Regulatory Plan of the most important significant regulatory actions reasonably expected to be issued; the Plan shall be approved by the agency head and shall contain at a minimum: (A) a statement of the agency's regulatory objectives and priorities and how they relate to the President's priorities; (B) a summary of each planned significant regulatory action including alternatives to be considered and preliminary estimates of anticipated costs and benefits; (C) a summary of the legal basis for each action, including whether any aspect is required by statute or court order; (D) a statement of the need for each action and, if applicable, how the action will reduce risks to public health, safety, or the environment and how the magnitude of the risk relates to other risks within the agency's jurisdiction; (E) the agency's schedule for action, including statutory or judicial deadlines; and (F) contact information for the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan requires senior sign-off and provides focused, public-facing summaries of significant planned actions and their analytic underpinnings; agencies must forward Plans to OIRA by June 1 each year and publish them in the October Unified Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency program to review existing significant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days of the Order, each agency shall submit to OIRA a program, consistent with its resources and priorities, under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any should be modified or eliminated to make the regulatory program more effective, less burdensome, or better aligned with the President's priorities; selected regulations for review shall be included in the agency's annual Plan; agencies shall also identify legislative mandates that require promulgation or continuation of regulations the agency believes are unnecessary or outdated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must proactively identify and review existing rules for elimination or modification and flag statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency public participation and comment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide the public with meaningful participation in the regulatory process; before issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, agencies should, where appropriate, seek the involvement of those intended to benefit from and those expected to be burdened by any regulation (including State, local, and tribal officials); afford the public a meaningful opportunity to comment on any proposed regulation, which in most cases should include a comment period of not less than 60 days; agencies are directed to explore and, where appropriate, use consensual mechanisms for developing regulations, including negotiated rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes early outreach, minimum 60-day comment periods in most cases, and use of collaborative rulemaking methods when suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Regulatory Policy Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the Order, each agency head shall designate a Regulatory Policy Officer who shall report to the agency head; the Officer shall be involved at each stage of the regulatory process to foster development of effective, innovative, and least burdensome regulations and to further the Order's principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an internal point of accountability within agencies for implementing the Order's principles across rulemaking stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency submission to OIRA — identification of planned actions and significance designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide OIRA with a list of its planned regulatory actions, indicating those which the agency believes are significant regulatory actions; absent a material change, those not designated significant will not be subject to review unless OIRA notifies the agency within 10 working days that OIRA has determined the planned regulation is a significant regulatory action; OIRA may waive review of any planned regulatory action designated by the agency as significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies self-identify significant actions but OIRA has a 10-working-day backstop to override; OIRA can also waive its review.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA submission requirements for significant actions — draft and basic assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: For each matter identified as, or determined by OIRA to be, a significant regulatory action, the issuing agency shall provide to OIRA: (i) the text of the draft regulatory action, together with a reasonably detailed description of the need for the regulatory action and an explanation of how the regulatory action will meet that need; and (ii) an assessment of the potential costs and benefits of the regulatory action, including an explanation of the manner in which the regulatory action is consistent with a statutory mandate and, to the extent permitted by law, promotes the President's priorities and avoids undue interference with State, local, and tribal governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These materials form the core of OIRA's review and must explain need, legal basis, and the agency's cost–benefit reasoning, including intergovernmental considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced analytic requirements for high‑impact actions (section 3(f)(1) scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters identified as, or determined to be, significant regulatory actions within the scope of section 3(f)(1), the agency shall also provide: (i) an assessment, including the underlying analysis, of benefits anticipated from the regulatory action together with, to the extent feasible, a quantification of those benefits; (ii) an assessment, including the underlying analysis, of costs anticipated from the regulatory action together with, to the extent feasible, a quantification of those costs; and (iii) an assessment, including the underlying analysis, of costs and benefits of potentially effective and reasonably feasible alternatives to the planned regulation and an explanation why the planned regulatory action is preferable to the identified potential alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-impact rules (e.g., $100M+ effects) require full analytic documentation of benefit/cost estimates and comparative analysis of feasible alternatives with justificatory explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and statutory-deadline exceptions for OIRA review
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergency situations or when an agency is obligated by law to act more quickly than normal review procedures allow, the agency shall notify OIRA as soon as possible and, to the extent practicable, comply with submission requirements; for regulatory actions governed by statutory or court-imposed deadlines, the agency shall, to the extent practicable, schedule proceedings to permit sufficient time for OIRA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility for truly time-sensitive actions while encouraging agencies to allow time for review when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication transparency by agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: After the regulatory action has been published in the Federal Register or otherwise issued to the public, the agency shall: (i) make available to the public the information set forth in submission requirements; (ii) identify for the public, in a complete, clear, and simple manner, the substantive changes between the draft submitted to OIRA for review and the action subsequently announced; and (iii) identify for the public those changes in the regulatory action that were made at the suggestion or recommendation of OIRA; all information provided to the public by the agency shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates public disclosure of OIRA-submitted materials, clear disclosure of changes and OIRA's role, and plain-language presentation to improve openness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review timelines and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall waive review or notify the agency in writing within: (A) 10 working days for notices of inquiry, advance notices of proposed rulemaking, or other preliminary regulatory actions prior to a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking; (B) 90 calendar days for all other regulatory actions after submission of required information unless previously reviewed (then 45 days); and (C) the review process may be extended once by no more than 30 calendar days upon written approval of the Director and at the request of the agency head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes predictable review clocks for OIRA while allowing a single short extension in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA returns and written explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each regulatory action that OIRA returns to an agency for further consideration of some or all of its provisions, the Administrator of OIRA shall provide the issuing agency a written explanation for such return, setting forth the pertinent provision of this Executive Order on which OIRA is relying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires reasoned, written feedback from OIRA when returning a draft, enabling an agency response or challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA disclosure and communications protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Administrator of OIRA (or a particular designee) shall receive oral communications initiated by persons not employed by the executive branch regarding the substance of a regulatory action under OIRA review; all substantive communications between OIRA personnel and outside persons shall: (i) invite a representative from the issuing agency to any meeting; (ii) be forwarded to the issuing agency within 10 working days if written; (iii) include dates and names of individuals involved in substantive oral communications; and (iv) be publicly disclosed as set forth (including maintaining a public log and making documents exchanged during review available after publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes strict handling, recordkeeping, and public-disclosure obligations for external communications with OIRA to increase transparency and include the issuing agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA public log and post-review document release
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall maintain a publicly available log that contains at a minimum: status of all regulatory actions (including Vice Presidential/Presidential consideration requests), notation of all written communications forwarded to issuing agencies, and dates/names of individuals involved in substantive oral communications and subject matter; after publication, OIRA shall make available to the public all documents exchanged between OIRA and the agency during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an auditable record of OIRA interactions and review status to facilitate public oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for agency and OIRA public information
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to the public by the agency and by OIRA shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency materials are accessible and reduces confusion around regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of interagency conflicts via Vice President/President
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreements or conflicts between or among agency heads or between OMB and any agency that cannot be resolved by the Administrator of OIRA shall be resolved by the President, or by the Vice President acting at the request of the President; Vice Presidential and Presidential consideration may be initiated only by the Director, the head of the issuing agency, or the head of an agency with a significant interest; the development of recommendations shall be concluded within 60 days after review is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes escalation to the highest executive levels for unresolved regulatory conflicts and a 60-day target for recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications during Vice Presidential/Presidential review must enter public docket
rubrics_metrics.description: During Vice Presidential and Presidential review, communications with any person not employed by the Federal Government relating to the substance of the regulatory action and directed to the Advisors or their staffs or to the staff of the Vice President shall be in writing and shall be forwarded by the recipient to the affected agency(ies) for inclusion in the public docket(s); when not in writing, staff shall inform the outside party that the matter is under review and that comments should be submitted in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that external inputs during high-level review are recorded in the public docket to preserve transparency and public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing restriction for actions subject to OIRA review
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent required by law, an agency shall not publish in the Federal Register or otherwise issue to the public any regulatory action that is subject to review under section 6 until (1) OIRA notifies the agency that it has waived review or has completed its review without requests for further consideration, or (2) the applicable time period in section 6(b)(2) expires without OIRA returning the action for further consideration, whichever occurs first; if the agency wishes to publish earlier, the head may request Presidential consideration through the Vice President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents agencies from circumventing OIRA review and keeps the sequence of internal review and public notice orderly; provides a pathway to seek Presidential permission to publish sooner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Working Group duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Order, the Administrator of OIRA shall convene a Regulatory Working Group consisting of representatives from agencies with significant domestic regulatory responsibility, the Advisors, and the Vice President; the Working Group shall assist agencies in identifying and analyzing important regulatory issues (including development of innovative regulatory techniques, methods and utility of comparative risk assessment, and development of streamlined approaches for small businesses), meet at least quarterly, and may commission analytical studies and reports by OIRA or other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an interagency forum to develop methodologies, share best practices, and address crosscutting regulatory issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of State/local/tribal assistance identifying burdensome regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: State, local, and tribal governments are specifically encouraged to assist in the identification of regulations that impose significant or unique burdens on them and that appear to have outlived their justification or be otherwise inconsistent with the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invites subfederal governments to participate in retrospective review and identification of rules for reform.
